review.material: All eight pages of the author-hosted text read, including Problems 1–15 and references.
review.limitations: Historical research agenda associated with the 1998 meeting and 2001 publication. No listed problem is asserted to remain open today; proposed solutions and cited constructions were not independently checked.

sections.title: Purpose of the paper
sections.text: A research agenda explaining what Borcherds found unsatisfactory or unexplained after the original moonshine theorem.

sections.title: Central questions
sections.text: Can the Monster vertex algebra be constructed more naturally? Can suitable integral forms connect its characteristic-zero and modular behavior? How far can moonshine extend?

sections.title: How problems are developed
sections.text: Each numbered question combines known constructions, a precise desired improvement and possible routes forward. Some proposals are deliberately speculative, especially links to geometry and physics.

sections.title: Examples of the agenda
sections.text: Problem 4 concerns commuting pairs rather than single group elements. Problems 6–8 seek classifications and natural realizations of generalized Kac–Moody algebras and related reflection groups.

sections.title: Outcome and how to use it
sections.text: The outcome is fifteen questions, not fifteen proved results or experiments. Read it to understand how anomalies become research programs; trace subsequent literature before treating any question as unresolved.
